div.head: SECT. 1.
MEMB. 2.
SUBSECT. 1.
Digression of Anatomy.
div.p: Before I proceed to define the Disease of Melancholy, what it is, or to discourse further of it, I hold it not impertinent to make a brief Digression of the anatomy of the body and faculties of the soul, for the better understanding of that which is to follow; because many hard words will often occur, as Mirach, Hypochondries, Haemorrhoids, &c., Imagination, Reason, Humours, Spirits, Vital, Natural, Animal, Nerves, Veins, Arteries, Chylus, Pituita; which of the vulgar will not so easily be perceived, what they are, how sited, and to what end they serve. And besides, it may peradventure give occasion to some men, to examine more accurately, search farther into this most excellent subject, and thereupon with that Royal Psal. 139. 14, 15.Prophet to praise God (for a man is fearfully and wonderfully made, and curiously wrought), that have time and leisure enough, & are sufficiently informed in all other worldly businesses, as to make a good bargain, buy and sell, to keep and make choice of a fair Hawk, Hound, Horse, &c. But for such matters as concern the knowledge of themselves, they are wholly ignorant and careless, they know not what this Body and Soul are, how combined, of what parts and faculties they consist, or how a man differs from a Dog. And what can be more ignominious and filthy (as De Anima.Melanchthon well inveighs) than for a man not to know the structure and composition of his own body, especially since the knowledge of it tends so much to the preservation of his health, and information of his manners? To stir them up therefore to this study, to peruse those elaborate works of De usu partium.Galen, Bauhinus, Plater, Vesalius, Fallopius, Laurentius, Remelinus, &c., which have written copiously in Latin; or that which some of our industrious Countrymen have done in our mother tongue, not long since, as that translation of History of man.Columbus, and Dr. Crooke.Microcosmographia, in 13 books, I have made this brief digression. Also because In Syntaxi.Wecker, De Anima.Melanchthon, Physiol. lib. 1, 2.Fernelius, Institut. lib. 1.Fuchsius, and those tedious Tracts de Anima [on the soul] (which have more compendiously handled & written of this matter) are not at all times ready to be had, to give them some small taste, or notice of the rest, let this Epitome suffice.
